summary: This article explains how robotic arms, cameras, and magnets at a recycling center sort plastic, paper, metal, and glass faster and more accurately than people can.
introduce: Read the title “Recycling Robots That Sort Our Trash” aloud and ask each student to write one question they hope the article will answer. Collect a few questions, then explain that today they will find the one big idea that ties all the details together.

keyTerms.def: a device that notices things like light, heat, or movement
a building or place built for a certain purpose
to make something dirty or mixed with the wrong material

challengeTerms.def: related to a kind of light that humans cannot see but that carries heat
a precise set of steps a computer follows to solve a problem or make a decision
able to continue for a long time without running out or causing lasting harm

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that robots will soon do most of the work of sorting our trash? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain how a robot identifies and sorts an item, and describe one limit of the system.
struggling: Pre-teach sensor, facility, and contaminate with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers complete a main-idea-and-details web with a partner.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses infrared, algorithm, and sustainable to state the main idea of the article in their own words.
